title: Every Polish group has a non-trivial topological group automorphism

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract asserts "every Polish group admits a non-trivial topological group automorphism", but Theorem 1.1 (and the whole argument) requires "more than two elements". The hypothesis is essential: the trivial group and Z_2 are Polish groups whose only automorphism is the identity. The unqualified abstract/title claim is therefore false and contradicts the theorem actually proved.

Theorem 3.1 states "A non-trivial Polish group cannot be uniquely homogeneous" (abstract: "there are no uniquely homogeneous Polish groups"). The two-element discrete group Z_2 is a non-trivial Polish group that IS uniquely homogeneous (for any p,q there is exactly one homeomorphism of the 2-point space taking p to q), and the one-point group is trivially uniquely homogeneous. Since the corollary is deduced from Theorem 1.1, which excludes groups with at most two elements, the statement must be restricted to groups with more than two elements.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Theorem 1.1 (choice of Y and definition of φ)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Y is only taken to be a maximal Z_2-linearly independent subset of U, and the only justification offered is that "every t ∈ U \ {0_G} is Z₂-linearly independent from {x_i}" (i.e. individual elements of U lie outside L). This does not give that Y ∪ {x_i} is linearly independent, i.e. span(Y) ∩ L = {0}, which is needed both for φ (identity on Y, non-trivial on span{x_i}) to be well defined on H and for the continuity argument "φ(U ∩ V) = U ∩ V" (which requires φ to fix U pointwise). The gap is fatal in concrete cases: for a connected Boolean Polish group (e.g. the measure algebra MALG, i.e. L^0([0,1],Z_2)) any identity neighbourhood U generates G, so span(Y) ⊇ span(U) = G ⊇ L, and the prescription φ(y)=y for y ∈ Y together with φ(x_0) ≠ x_0 is contradictory.

The text writes "(x + V′) + (y + V′) = ∅ if x, y ∈ L are distinct" and later "(x + V′) + (y + V′) ⊆ (x + x + U_x) ∩ (y + y + U_y) = ∅". The set sum of two non-empty sets is never empty, and the displayed line mixes the group operation + with intersection ∩; the intended (and needed) statement is (x + V′) ∩ (y + V′) = ∅. As written the step is mathematically false/incoherent.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3 (discussion before Question 3.3) vs. proof of Theorem 1.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 3 says "we use its Kuratowski-Zorn version in Lemma 2.3 to construct the identity neighbourhood U and the axiom of choice itself when finding a maximal Z₂-linearly independent subset Y ⊆ U", but the proof of Theorem 1.1 explicitly states "With the Kuratowski–Zorn lemma we can construct a maximal Z₂-linearly independent subset Y ⊆ U". The two passages attribute the construction of Y to different choice principles.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, paragraph on mapping class groups (reference [4])
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The blanket claim that for extended mapping class groups of (connected) metrizable surfaces "every algebraic automorphism is faithfully represented by a conjugation with a mapping class" and that "every extended mapping class group is naturally isomorphic to its automorphism group" ignores the well-known low-complexity exceptions (e.g. the closed genus-2 surface, whose mapping class group has a non-trivial centre, so the conjugation representation is not faithful; the torus and spheres with few punctures are likewise exceptional in Ivanov-type theorems). The cited results hold only with such exclusions.
